result.summary: The image depicts a wide multi-lane roadway with sidewalks on both sides, set in a mixed-use commercial and institutional area. While sidewalks are continuous, the environment is heavily oriented toward motor vehicles, featuring long crossing distances at the distant intersection and no visible mid-block pedestrian protections.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The multi-lane configuration and wide asphalt surface encourage high vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the road at the intersection ahead creates a long exposure time for pedestrians crossing multiple lanes of traffic.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes to slow traffic and reallocate space for protected bike lanes or wider pedestrian buffers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the faint transverse markings at the intersection to high-visibility continental markings.

result.summary: This is a residential mid-block environment featuring row houses and parallel on-street parking. While sidewalks and a painted bike lane are present, there is no physical protection for vulnerable road users from motor vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles obscures the visibility of pedestrians, especially children, who might attempt to cross the street mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway where cars are parked.

hazards.name: Unprotected Bike Lane
hazards.description: The bike lane is only demarcated by paint and is located in the 'door zone' of parked cars, creating risks for cyclists and indirectly for pedestrians if cyclists swerve into the walkway area.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Installing physical traffic calming measures to ensure low vehicle speeds in this residential context.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Adding vertical delineators or moving the parking lane to the outside of the bike lane to provide physical separation.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, two-lane urban street with continuous sidewalks and parallel on-street parking. The environment lacks dedicated pedestrian safety features such as marked crosswalks or traffic calming measures, which may encourage higher vehicle speeds and create difficult crossing conditions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks in this mid-block section, requiring pedestrians to cross unprotected across multiple lanes.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Marked Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Add a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated and safer space for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds on this straight stretch of road, improving safety for all users.

result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban pedestrian environment with a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk separated from the roadway by a curb and parallel parking. The environment is functional but lacks high-quality pedestrian amenities such as street trees, buffers, or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is positioned within the sidewalk zone, which, while not blocking the path entirely, reduces the effective clear width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the sidewalk in front of the stone building.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Installing street trees or a planting strip would provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, improving pedestrian comfort and safety.
